slides.2.title: 🥩 Tuscany in Depth: Beyond the Basics, into the Details
slides.2.content:
Level 1 introduced Chianti with tomato sauce and steak. Level 2 goes further: within Tuscany, Brunello, Vino Nobile and Vernaccia di San Gimignano each have their ideal partners — choose wrongly and the wine is wasted.

🍷 Brunello / Vino Nobile

Bistecca alla Fiorentina 2.0: if Chianti is the first choice for an everyday steak, Brunello di Montalcino is the top choice for a dry-aged T-bone — a longer finish for deeper meat flavours.
Wild boar stew (cinghiale): the elegant tannins of Vino Nobile di Montepulciano with the wild flavour of boar give more layers than Chianti.
White truffle (tartufo bianco): the tobacco and earth of aged Brunello echo the complexity of truffle — the epitome of a luxury pairing.

🥂 Vernaccia / Vin Santo

Vernaccia di San Gimignano + steamed white fish: Tuscany's only white DOCG, whose minerality suits Mediterranean-style white fish, the best example of central Italian seafood pairing.
Vin Santo + cantucci (almond biscuits): Tuscany's most traditional dessert pairing — dip cantucci in Vin Santo, the purest expression of local culture. The wine is sweeter than the biscuits, fully following the sweetness rule.
slides.3.title: 🐗 Marche & Umbria: Verdicchio, King of Seafood + Sagrantino, the Wild Red
slides.3.content:
Marche is coastal, Umbria is inland and mountainous — two neighbouring regions whose different landscapes create very different food cultures, and so very different pairing logic

🐟 Marche: Brodetto di Pesce (fish stew)

The Adriatic tomato and seafood stew is the soul of Marche. Verdicchio dei Castelli di Jesi is the absolute first choice — its minerality echoes the shellfish and its high acidity balances the tomato, a textbook case of Italian seafood pairing. Verdicchio is also recommended with steamed sea bass.

🐇 Marche: Coniglio in Porchetta (herb-roasted rabbit)

A homely Marche dish, slow-roasted with herbs, rosemary and garlic. Rosso Piceno (a Montepulciano + Sangiovese blend) has a moderate body for white meat, or a light Verdicchio works too — rabbit is delicate and needs a partner that doesn't steal the show.

🐗 Umbria: Sagrantino + Wild Boar Stew

Sagrantino di Montefalco ranks among Italy's most tannic grapes and needs the strongest dishes to tame it. Umbria's mountain wild boar stew (cinghiale) is its natural partner — high tannin binds with meat protein, wild with wild. After several years of ageing it shows even more depth.

🖤 Umbria: Tartufo Nero (black truffle)

Umbria is Italy's most important black truffle area (Norcia). The earth and tobacco of aged Sagrantino echo black truffle's earthiness, and Orvieto Classico white also suits black-truffle butter pasta — the white's freshness avoids overwhelming the truffle's delicate aroma.
slides.4.title: ☀️ Campania & the South: Seafood, Spice and Rich Reds
slides.4.content:
Campania has ancient grapes such as Fiano and Greco that match seafood and pizza precisely; Puglia's Primitivo and Negroamaro take on grilled meats without hesitation. Southern food is rich and spicy and needs equally full wines.

🍕 Campania

Neapolitan pizza + Fiano di Avellino: Fiano's peach-stone and hazelnut notes with Neapolitan tomato sauce are more true to Campania than Chianti.
Seafood pasta + Greco di Tufo: the minerality from volcanic soils echoes the briny savour of seafood — Campania's signature pairing.
Spaghetti alle vongole (clam spaghetti) + Lacryma Christi Bianco: a white from the foot of Vesuvius whose mineral, salty savour echoes the seafood — the most authentic local match.

🍖 Puglia & Basilicata

Grilled lamb chops + Primitivo di Manduria: Primitivo's sweet black fruit with the smoky char of grilled lamb is the most common combination on Puglian farm tables.
Orecchiette con cime di rapa (ear-shaped pasta with bitter greens) + Negroamaro: the slight bitterness of the greens with Negroamaro's herbal bitterness — local wisdom of bitter with bitter.
Aglianico del Vulture + lamb and chickpea stew: Basilicata's mountain red with a mountain stew, a perfect regional pairing.
slides.5.title: 🏝️ Sicily & Sardinia: Volcanoes, Sea and the Soul of the Mediterranean
slides.5.content:
Sicily's volcanic soils and Mediterranean climate create wines of strong character; Sardinia's Cannonau and Vermentino are inseparable from the island's pastoral culture and seafood.

🌋 Sicily: Volcanic Character with Mediterranean Food

Nero d'Avola + grilled tuna steak (tonno alla griglia)

Tuna is the "red meat of the sea", and the rich black fruit of Nero d'Avola with its meaty texture is a traditional pairing in Sicilian fishing ports. The volcanic minerality of Etna Rosso adds layers with grilled meat.

🐙 Sicily: Sweet-and-Sour Dishes

Caponata (sweet-and-sour aubergine) + Insolia / Grillo (whites)

Sicilian sweet-and-sour sauces need a dry white for balance; Grillo's fresh acidity answers the aubergine, olive and vinegar sauce. The same goes for sarde a beccafico (stuffed sardines), with the high acid and minerality of Etna Bianco.

🐑 Sardinia: Roast Lamb and Cannonau

Porceddu (roast suckling pig) / spit-roast lamb + Cannonau di Sardegna

Cannonau (Grenache) is Sardinia's main red, full of fruit with soft tannins, perfect with the island's roast suckling pig and lamb — the most direct expression of its pastoral culture.

🐟 Sardinia: Seafood with Vermentino

Roast sea bass (branzino) + Vermentino di Gallura DOCG

Vermentino di Gallura is Sardinia's only DOCG white, its sea-breeze minerality mirroring the sweetness of sea fish — the model local pairing of "sea breeze with sea fish".
slides.6.title: 🎓 Key Takeaways
slides.6.points.0: ✓ Tuscany in detail: Chianti with an everyday steak, Brunello with a top steak, Vino Nobile with wild boar; Vin Santo with dipped cantucci is the most local dessert pairing
slides.6.points.1: ✓ Verdicchio dei Castelli di Jesi is the textbook match for Marche's fish stew — minerality + high acid perfectly answer tomato and seafood
slides.6.points.2: ✓ Sagrantino di Montefalco ranks among Italy's most tannic grapes and needs strong dishes such as wild boar stew
slides.6.points.3: ✓ Campania: Fiano di Avellino with Neapolitan pizza, Greco di Tufo with seafood — ancient local grapes find local southern food
slides.6.points.4: ✓ Orecchiette con cime di rapa (ear-shaped pasta with bitter greens) with Negroamaro — the contrasting wisdom of bitter with bitter, Puglia's most traditional pairing
slides.6.points.5: ✓ Sicily: Nero d'Avola with grilled tuna — tuna is the red meat of the sea and can take a full red
slides.6.points.6: ✓ Sardinia: Cannonau with roast lamb (an expression of pastoral culture); Vermentino di Gallura with roast sea bass (sea breeze with sea fish)
slides.6.points.7: ✓ The core of central and southern pairing: the richer the dish, the fuller the wine; food from the same island or region looks first to wine from the same region
slides.7.title: 🧠 Central, Southern and Island Pairing Knowledge Check
slides.7.questions.0.question: Which pairing for Marche's brodetto di pesce (tomato and seafood stew) best follows the regional principle?
slides.7.questions.0.options.1: B. Verdicchio dei Castelli di Jesi (Marche white)
slides.7.questions.0.explanation: Verdicchio is a native Marche grape whose minerality perfectly echoes the Adriatic seafood and whose high acidity stands up to the tomato — a textbook local pairing.
slides.7.questions.1.question: Why must Sagrantino di Montefalco be paired with rich dishes such as wild boar stew rather than delicate white fish?
slides.7.questions.1.options.0: A. Sagrantino is too dark and doesn't look right with white fish
slides.7.questions.1.options.1: B. Sagrantino ranks among Italy's most tannic grapes, and delicate food cannot balance its strong astringency
slides.7.questions.1.options.2: C. Sagrantino must be drunk in Umbria
slides.7.questions.1.options.3: D. Sagrantino is too sweet and seems odd with fish
slides.7.questions.1.explanation: Sagrantino's very high tannin needs meat protein to bind with and soften it; delicate white fish lacks protein and fat, making Sagrantino's astringency even more pronounced and hard to drink. The weights must match.
slides.7.questions.2.question: What is the most authentic pairing for Sardinian roast sea bass (branzino al forno)?
slides.7.questions.2.explanation: Vermentino di Gallura is Sardinia's only DOCG white, whose sea-breeze minerality perfectly mirrors the sweet freshness of roast sea bass — "sea breeze with sea fish" is the model of regional pairing.
slides.7.questions.3.question: Which wine best suits Sicilian caponata (sweet-and-sour aubergine)?
slides.7.questions.3.options.2: C. Grillo or Insolia (dry Sicilian whites)
slides.7.questions.3.explanation: Caponata is sweet and sour and needs the acidity of a dry white to balance the vinegar and sweetness, not a sweet wine (adding sweetness) or a heavy red (smothering the delicate sauce). Grillo/Insolia are native Sicilian white grapes, following the regional principle.
slides.7.questions.4.question: Which of these are correct central and southern Italian pairings? (Select all that apply)
slides.7.questions.4.options.0: A. Vin Santo (sweet wine) with dipped cantucci (almond biscuits) — a traditional Tuscan dessert pairing
slides.7.questions.4.options.1: B. Puglia's orecchiette with bitter greens and Negroamaro (a bitter-with-bitter contrast)
slides.7.questions.4.options.2: C. Campania's Fiano di Avellino with Neapolitan seafood pasta
slides.7.questions.4.options.3: D. Brunello di Montalcino with a Neapolitan Margherita pizza
slides.7.questions.4.explanation: Vin Santo is sweeter than cantucci, following the sweetness rule; Negroamaro's herbal bitterness echoes the bitter greens, the wisdom of bitter contrast; Fiano's mineral fruit suits seafood perfectly. Brunello is too full and would overwhelm the tomato and cheese of a Margherita, and comes from a different region — choose Chianti or Fiano instead.
quiz.0.question: Which pairing for Marche's tomato and seafood stew best follows the regional principle?
quiz.0.explanation: Verdicchio's minerality echoes the seafood and its high acidity stands up to the tomato — Marche's most local pairing.
quiz.1.question: Why is Sagrantino unsuited to delicate white fish?
quiz.1.options.1: Its tannin is very high and delicate food cannot balance its astringency
quiz.1.options.2: It must be drunk in Umbria
quiz.1.explanation: Sagrantino's very high tannin needs protein to bind with, and delicate white fish cannot handle it.
quiz.2.question: What is the most authentic pairing for Sardinian roast sea bass?
quiz.2.explanation: Vermentino di Gallura's sea-breeze minerality mirrors the sweet freshness of sea fish — the model of "sea breeze with sea fish".
quiz.3.question: What is the most traditional dessert pairing for Tuscan Vin Santo?
quiz.3.options.2: Cantucci almond biscuits (dipped in Vin Santo)
quiz.3.explanation: Dipping cantucci in Vin Santo is Tuscany's most traditional local dessert culture, fully following the sweetness rule.
